QuestionStmt.S: Which among the following compounds has lowest boiling point?

Solution.S:
Boiling point depends on intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonding, van der Waals forces).

- $(\mathrm{C_2H_5})_2\mathrm{NH}$ (diethylamine) has hydrogen bonding (N–H).
- $\mathrm{C_2H_5N(CH_3)_2}$ (tertiary amine) has no N–H bond, hence no intermolecular hydrogen bonding → lowest boiling point.
- $n-\mathrm{C_4H_9OH}$ (butanol) has strong hydrogen bonding (O–H).
- $\mathrm{C_2H_5COOH}$ (propanoic acid) has strong hydrogen bonding (dimer formation).

Thus the compound with the lowest boiling point is $\mathrm{C_2H_5N(CH_3)_2}$, which corresponds to option B.
